4.02.b:
### TFCC — parts & attachments
[[FIG: Fig 4.5 · 4.02
- Insertion → **deep fibres → fovea**, superficial → styloid

MUST-KNOW — "iceberg" of the TFCC
- Distal "hammock" = disc + ulnocarpal ligaments → load cushion (Nakamura 1996)
- Proximal part → **foveal insertion** = the real DRUJ stabiliser (Atzei 2011)
- Foveal tear → severe DRUJ instability, even with a normal-looking disc (Nakamura 2011)
- Styloid tip fracture → foveal fibres usually spared; **base** fracture → suspect the fovea
- **Fovea sign** → tender soft spot between ulnar styloid, FCU and pisiform → foveal TFCC (1B) or UT ligament (Netter; Hanna; Nagah)

### Blood supply & the Palmer zones
- Disc → avascular, aneural; periphery vascular (ulnar + anterior interosseous arteries)
  [[FIG: Fig 4.6 · 4.02
- Rule → **peripheral tear repair · central tear debride**
- Palmer 1 (traumatic) → 1A central perforation (debride) · 1B ulnar avulsion (repair) · 1C ulnocarpal ligaments · 1D radial avulsion
- Class 2 = degenerative (ulnocarpal impaction)

PITFALL — how much of the TFCC bleeds?
- Netter → outer 10–25%; Thiru 1986 → outer 15–20%
- Say → "**the outer fifth bleeds**, the centre does not"

### Point & say — the 8 carpal bones
- Proximal row, radial → ulnar → **S**caphoid · **L**unate · **T**riquetrum · **P**isiform
  [[FIG: Fig 4.8 · 4.03
- Distal row → **T**rapezium · **T**rapezoid · **C**apitate · **H**amate
- Mnemonic → "**S**ome **L**overs **T**ry **P**ositions **T**hat **T**hey **C**an't **H**andle"

| Bone | Hold it → say |
|---|---|
| Scaphoid | Boat-shaped, **80% cartilage**, bridges both rows → #1 carpal fracture, waist ≈66% |
| Lunate | Crescent, 4 joints (radius, scaphoid, triquetrum, capitate) |
| Triquetrum | Pyramid under the pisiform → 3rd commonest carpal fracture |
| Pisiform | Sesamoid in **FCU** (flexor carpi ulnaris) → TCL (transverse carpal ligament), ADM (abductor digiti minimi) |
| Trapezium | Groove for **FCR** (flexor carpi radialis); saddle for the thumb |
| Capitate | Largest, first to ossify, keystone, centre of rotation |
| Hamate | **Hook** → TCL; deep ulnar nerve on it |

- Find the hook → thumb IP (interphalangeal) crease on the pisiform, tip toward the 1st web → hook under it

- **Counter-clockwise from the capitate**, about one a year → capitate 1 → hamate 2 → triquetrum 3 → lunate 4 → scaphoid 5 → trapezium 5–6 → trapezoid 6–7 → **pisiform 9–10**

4.04.b:
### Extrinsic ligaments
- **Palmar** ligaments stronger, intracapsular; dorsal ones converge on the triquetrum
  [[FIG: Fig 4.12 · 4.04

| Group | Ligament | Point & say |
|---|---|---|
| Volar superficial | **RSC** | Styloid → capitate; scaphoid waist **sling** |
| Volar superficial | **LRL** (long radiolunate) | Radius → lunate; proximal border of Poirier |
| Volar deep | **Ligament of Testut** | Radioscapholunate → vessels only, no strength |
| Dorsal | **DRC** (dorsal radiocarpal) | Radius → triquetrum → main dorsal stabiliser |
| Dorsal | **DIC** (dorsal intercarpal) | Triquetrum → trapezium/trapezoid → forms the dorsal "**V**" with DRC |

- **Space of Poirier** → weak area between LRL and RSC + UC (ulnocapitate) at the capitate neck → **perilunate dislocations pass here**

### Intrinsic ligaments
- **SL** (scapholunate) → C-shaped → **dorsal part strongest** · **LT** (lunotriquetral) → **palmar part strongest**
  [[FIG: Fig 4.13 · 4.04

MUST-KNOW — SL or LT? DISI or VISI?
- SL torn → scaphoid flexes, lunate **extends** → **DISI** (dorsal intercalated segment instability)
- LT + DRC torn → lunate **flexes** with the scaphoid → **VISI** (volar intercalated segment instability) (Netter)
- Static DISI → needs SL **+ DIC** off the lunate; SL cut alone not enough (Mitsuyasu 2004)
- Memory → "**S**L → lunate looks up (D) · **L**T → lunate looks down (V)"

### Rows, columns & motion
- Proximal row → **no tendon attachments** → **intercalated segment** moved by the rows around it
  [[FIG: Fig 4.14 · 4.04
- **Dart-thrower's motion** → radial-extension to ulnar-flexion, all midcarpal → functional plane

1) SL torn
[[FIG: Fig 4.15 · 4.04
2) Lunocapitate → capitate dislocates
3) LT torn → perilunate dislocation
4) Lunate dislocates volarly **through the space of Poirier**

- **Lesser arc** = pure ligament · **greater arc** = through bone → transscaphoid perilunate is the commonest
